title: Banded KV striping and fused attention heuristics - sketch
content:
Purpose
This is a working sketch exploring an alternative to the current paged-KV layout: banded KV striping. Goal is to reduce hot-spotting on L2 and SM shared memory during bursty long-context queries and make fused-attn kernels more bandwidth-friendly when doing FlashAttention-style multi-block attention.

High-level idea
- Instead of a single contiguous page per KV object, split large KV pages into small 'bands' that are independently addressable and can be striped across multiple GPU memory channels and memory pools.
- At runtime we select a stripe width and band placement based on inferred access patterns (prefix reuse vs long-tail random access).
- Combine banded layout with a fusion path that groups layernorm->qkv->flash-attn into one CUDA kernel when the sequence length and batch shape match the banding layout.

Motivation and observations from perf experiments
- Long tokens with heavy prefix reuse saturate certain L2 paths; contiguous pages cause repeated loads of the same L2 lines and thrash per-SM caches.
- FlashAttention gets worse when KV fetches are serialized across many warps that hit the same memory channel. Banding can interleave accesses to reduce hot lanes.
- Microbatching amplifies the problem: many small requests hitting the same KV offsets at slightly different time slices create temporal locality that L2 cannot exploit effectively.

Banding model details
- Band size candidates: 16KB, 64KB, 256KB per band. Tune by GPU model.
- Stripe factor: number of distinct memory pools or banks we rotate bands across. Typical values 2..8.
- Placement policies: round-robin, hot-cold heuristic (place cold bands in high-latency pool to free hot pool), and adaptive rebalance based on miss counters.
- Metadata: store small per-page band bitset and last-access timestamps in host-managed metadata table (packed 32-bit entries). Keep metadata small to keep lookup cheap.

Runtime path and API hooks
- On allocation: allocate N bands for the KV object and register them with the allocator with stripe hints.
- On read: compute band id = floor(offset / band_size) and route load to GPU pointer for that band. Prefetch logic can populate one or more bands into L2 via warm-up loads or prefetch kernel.
- Eviction: evict entire bands, not individual cache lines. This simplifies paging and reduces bookkeeping.

Fusion opportunities with FlashAttention
- Constraint: Fusion is only profitable if the fused kernel can read consecutive QKV tiles that align with band boundaries to maximize coalescing.
- Strategy: create a two-level tiler inside fused kernel. Outer tiler iterates over bands assigned to this request. Inner tiler runs FlashAttention over tiles inside the band.
- Benefit: when multiple streams read different bands, memory controller interleaving reduces per-band contention and the fused kernel can still do warp-level cooperations for softmax and KV accumulation.

Kernel sketch (pseudocode)
- Host allocation and band registration:
  for each KV_object:
    bands = ceil(size / band_size)
    for b in 0..bands-1:
      gpu_ptr = allocator.alloc(band_size, stripe_hint=(obj_id + b) % stripe_factor)
      register_band(obj_id, b, gpu_ptr)

- Fused kernel launch (per microbatch chunk):
  for band in assigned_bands:
    load_band_metadata(band)
    for tile in tiles_in_band:
      load_qkv_tile_coalesced(tile)
      flashattn_local(tile)   // single kernel does qkv->attn->out for that tile

Performance heuristics and knobs
- When seq_len < 512, prefer no-banding; fusion without banding is simpler and often faster due to simpler indexing.
- For seq_len in 512..4096, band_size=64KB, stripe=4 often gives good balance for A100/RTX-class cards in our internal perf tests.
- For very large contexts (>16K tokens), increase band_size to 256KB to reduce metadata overhead.
- Eviction threshold: trigger band eviction when free GPU memory below 12% or when per-band LRU age > T where T is workload-specific (default 30s).

Prefetch policies
- Prefix prefetch: when a request indicates strong prefix reuse, prefetch first N bands synchronously to reduce first-token latency.
- Lazy prefetch: for background/batch requests, prefetch one band at a time and overlap with compute.
- Cooperative prefetch: use a small prefetch scheduler per-GPU that tries to coalesce prefetches across concurrent requests to amortize bandwidth.

Tradeoffs and open questions
- Metadata scaling: per-band metadata increases host memory and lookup complexity. How to compress or shard metadata cheaply? Could use bloom filters per-object to approximate hot bands.
- Failure modes: bad stripe choices may increase cross-channel contention if hardware interleaves differently than expected. Need hw-specific autotune.
- Integration with existing paged-KV: plan is to keep paged-KV compatibility layer; most code paths treat band as contiguous for eviction and snapshots.
- Compiler support: fused kernel relies on compile-time constants for band_size in some paths. We should provide templated kernels and a small runtime JIT or NVRTC compile step for uncommon combos.

Experiments to run
- Microbench 1: uniform random accesses across 1M-token KV with and without banding. Measure SM utilization, L2 hit rate, latency p50/p99.
- Microbench 2: prefix-heavy workload with 128 concurrent streams. Evaluate eviction churn and prefetch effectiveness.
- Macrobench: run RLHF-style rollout where context grows; measure end-to-end throughput and cost per token.

Implementation plan (phases)
- Phase 0: simulation and allocator changes. Implement banded allocator prototype in user-space allocator with no kernel fusion.
- Phase 1: prefetch scheduler + eviction by band. Add metrics and instrumentation.
- Phase 2: fused kernel prototypes for A100 and H100, with band-aligned tiling and autotune profiles.
- Phase 3: conservative rollout behind a config flag and A/B evaluation on Dedicated clusters.

TODOs and action items
- Lukas: prototype host-side band metadata table and allocator hook. Blocker: need allocator API changes by Nov 15.
- Maya: write microbench 1 harness and collect baseline numbers for A100 by Nov 22.
- Nina: evaluate NVRTC compile overhead for generated fused kernels and estimate runtime overheads.
- Jordan: draft Confluence page linking results and scheduling heuristics.

Notes to reviewers
- This is a sketch, not a final design. Focus review on the feasibility of band eviction and interaction with flash-attn fusion. Questions on hardware-specific interleaving and autotune are high priority.
- If this looks promising, I will prepare a deeper RFC with pseudocode and benchmark artifacts.

End of sketch.
